title: Transform
definition: The `transform` CSS property lets you rotate, scale, skew, or translate an element. It modifies the coordinate space of the CSS visual formatting model.
simpleExplanation: It's a way to physically manipulate a box without breaking the layout of the webpage. If you use `margin-top: 50px` to move a box down, you push everything else on the page down too. If you use `transform: translateY(50px)`, the box visually moves down, but it leaves a 'ghost' behind, so the rest of the webpage doesn't move an inch.
realWorldExample: Using `transform: scale(1.1)` on a button hover to make it pop out at the user without pushing the surrounding text away.
useCases: High-performance animations (60 FPS GPU hardware acceleration)

basic: Why is animating `transform` better than animating `margin` or `top`?
intermediate: Can you apply multiple transforms at the same time?

answers.question: Why is it better?
answers.answer: Performance. Changing margins or widths causes the browser to recalculate the entire page layout (Reflow), which is incredibly CPU heavy and causes stuttering. `transform` is handed off directly to the GPU (Graphics Card), making the animation a buttery smooth 60 Frames Per Second.

answers.question: Multiple transforms?
answers.answer: Yes! You chain them together separated by a space. Example: `transform: scale(1.5) rotate(45deg);`.
